summary: Intermittent 429s for dedicated tenant only when X-Client-Trace header is present
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports persistent 429 responses for some requests originating from their orchestration layer. Pattern: 429s appear only when requests include an X-Client-Trace header and occur across multiple client hosts but only for the dedicated pool assigned to Nightingale Analytics. Impact: interrupts nightly analytics jobs and causes partial data-loss retries. Scope: ~12% of requests from their uploader cluster returned 429 over a 3-hour window on 2024-09-14.

Observed behavior: customer receives 429 with standard throttle headers (x-rw-ratelimit-remaining: 0) but console shows tenant credits remaining. Throttles stop when tracing header stripped by a local proxy.

Why this ticket: narrow, reproducible correlation between specific request header and route-layer accounting leading to double-counting across route and tenant layers. Customer requested explanation and workaround while we investigate permanent fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In dedicated tenant Nightingale Analytics, send a steady stream (200rps) of small chat requests to /v1/chat/completions with API key for their dedicated pool.
2) Include header: X-Client-Trace: trace-<uuid> on a subset (~20%) of requests while keeping HTTP/2 persistent connections enabled.
3) Observe 429s start after ~15 minutes for requests with tracing header while other requests succeed.
4) Repeat but remove X-Client-Trace header — throttles disappear immediately.
5) Attach gateway logs and x-rw-* throttle headers for proof points.
logs: [09:12:07] gateway-01 us-west | req_id=abc123 path=/v1/chat status=429 x-rw-ratelimit-remaining=0 x-rw-ratelimit-reset=1694788807 X-Client-Trace=trace-7b2f
[09:12:08] gateway-02 us-west | req_id=abc124 path=/v1/chat status=200 x-rw-ratelimit-remaining=12
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: header influenced fingerprint algorithm causing a single incoming HTTP/2 connection to be counted multiple times at route layer because the tracer header changes per request while connection reuse causes tenant-layer counting to use api-key only, resulting in misaligned windows and earlier route exhaustion. Reproduced in staging with customer's request pattern. Instrumented rate-limiter to log fingerprint components; confirmed that requests containing X-Client-Trace produced a route fingerprint which included the header value, making each traced request appear unique at route scope while tenant scope still aggregated by API key. This triggered a route-level token burn that did not match tenant consumption metrics shown in console.

Further notes: Problem surfaced after a recent gateway change (PR 487) that began including all non-standard headers in fingerprinting by default to mitigate certain replay attacks. That change did not consider high-cardinality tracing headers.
customer_communication: 2024-09-15 09:30 UTC - Support (Aisha): Thanks for the data — we see correlation between X-Client-Trace and 429s. Can you confirm if your uploader uses HTTP/2 keepalive?
2024-09-15 09:36 UTC - Customer (Nightingale): Yes - our orchestrator multiplexes many short requests over a few persistent HTTP/2 connections. Removing the tracing header fixed it in our quick test.

2024-09-15 11:05 UTC - SRE (Marco): Instrumented rate-limiter and confirmed header included in route fingerprint. Creating hotfix to exclude tracing headers from fingerprint. Will deploy a canary in us-west-2.
2024-09-16 02:15 UTC - SRE (Marco): Canary deployed to 10% of gateways in us-west-2. No further 429s observed for traced requests in canary. Proceeding to full rollout.
2024-09-18 14:20 UTC - Support (Aisha): Fix deployed globally and we backfilled route accounting window alignment. Customer validated overnight run — no throttles. Closing ticket with follow-ups.
resolution: Hotfix rolled: changed default fingerprinting config to ignore header names matching ^X-Client-Trace$ and other high-cardinality tracing headers. Deployed canary on 2024-09-16 then full rollout 2024-09-17. Backfilled route-layer refill state for affected tenant to remove residual negative window drift. Recommended customer guidance: for now avoid per-request high-cardinality headers on dedicated pools, or set tracing as an allowed header but client-side stable value (same trace per connection) until we shipped config UI to exclude headers. Follow-up tasks created: INT-2110 (add admin toggle for ignored-fingerprint-headers) and INT-2111 (add telemetry alert for high-cardinality header detection).
follow_up_actions: INT-2110: Admin UI to configure ignored-fingerprint-headers (owner: product infra)
INT-2111: High-cardinality header detection & alerting (owner: observability)
SUP-314420: Inform customers about header best-practices for dedicated pools (owner: Customer Docs)
Internal postmortem scheduled in Confluence: runbook link provided
notes_for_support: If customers report similar 429 spikes, ask whether they send transient per-request headers (traces, per-request session ids) over HTTP/2 with connection reuse. Temporary mitigation: strip or normalize header at edge or add header to ignored-fingerprint list via support request. Use PR 512 as reference for the hotfix.
